newsitem.title: MEXICO: Alleged rebel arrests rise to 22 in Mexican state.
newsitem.headline: Alleged rebel arrests rise to 22 in Mexican state.

text.p: Mexican police and army units have arrested 22 alleged leftist guerrillas in the southern state of Oaxaca over the last two days, officials said Friday.
Oaxaca state prosecutor Roberto Martinez, who announced the arrest of 14 suspected members of the leftist Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) Thursday, said that the total had now risen to 22.
Two of the arrests were on firearms charges, one on a charge of murder and the rest for membership of the rebel group, he said.
The arrests took place in and around the Pacific coast Loxicha area of the mountainous state, one of Mexico's poorest.

Those arrested are believed to have taken part in the rebel group's biggest attacks to date, on Aug. 28 this year, when coordinated strikes against army and police units in several states killed at least 15 people, officials said.
The Mexican Human Rights Defence League said Thursday that according to its information, the total of arrests and disappearances during the counterinsurgency operations was closer to 40.
The hardline leftist EPR appeared for the first time in June this year in the southern state of Guerrero and has since carried out attacks and propaganda operations in nine states.
